content.statement: A request is granted on behalf of a user only if its token belongs to that user and the user is authorized.
content.why: Users identify themselves with tokens they receive at login, so a decision sees a token, not a user. abs: a user is allowed a resource when some token of theirs is granted it.

DecisionContract.reason: Checked on every call; the examples show it grants and refuses as the idea says.

content.statement: A decision names the user its token belongs to, and only when a grant covers the path.
content.why: GrantBased, stated for one call, so every result of the running system can be checked.

sources.post: (token, path, decision) => decision.forall(u => sessions(token) == Some(u) && grants.value.contains(Grant(u, path)))

examples: expect ("t1", Path("/a")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants = ::(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")), List()), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — Alice's token and a grant for /a: she gets in
expect ("t1", Path("/b")) ⇒ None  given grants = ::(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")), List()), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — no grant for /b: refused

reject ("t1", Path("/b")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants = ::(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")), List()), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — access without a grant is never given

reject ("t2", Path("/a")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants = ::(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a")), List()), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — a token that is not Alice's never acts for her

InMemorySessions.reason: One instance today; revisit when we scale out.

content.statement: Sessions and grants are held in memory, in one process; a decision is one map lookup and one set lookup.
content.why: One service decides access, and the tables fit in memory. A shared store would only be needed with several instances.

NoUnauthorizedAccess.reason: This is the sentence of the idea that must never be broken.

content.statement: A user is never granted access to a resource they are not authorized to access.
content.why: This is the one thing the idea says must never happen. What 'authorized' means is left open: the idea only fixes it later, as grants.

content.idea:
# Auth

A system decides which users may access which resources. No user may ever
access a resource they are not authorized to access.

Users identify themselves with tokens they receive at login. Authorization is
given by a table of grants: a user may access a path when a grant names that
user and that path.
